faqs.question: What are good categories for a Halloween costume contest?
faqs.answer: Pick five to eight awards that fit the setting rather than the classic scariest-funniest pair. An office might use The Out-of-Office Award, Reply-All Horror and a Best Effort Badge, while a virtual contest suits The Frame Filler and The Mute Button Mime.

faqs.question: How many award categories does a costume contest need?
faqs.answer: Roughly one award for every four to six people in costume, capped at eight. Fewer awards than that and one friend group wins everything; more and the prizes stop meaning much.

faqs.question: What are some funny costume contest award names?
faqs.answer: Try The Quarterly Pun Report for wordplay, The Commute Survivor for a costume that arrived intact, or The Buffering Award for a glitch-themed outfit on a video call. All 36 names in this guide are original, so you can use them freely.

faqs.question: Is approval voting better than a single vote for a costume contest?
faqs.answer: For rooms of 20 or more, usually yes. A 2002 field trial in France found approval voting easy to understand and well accepted, and it changed the ranking compared with a single-choice vote, because people can back several entries at once instead of picking between loyalty and craft.

faqs.question: How do I stop a costume contest becoming a popularity contest?
faqs.answer: Use entry numbers instead of names, ban voting for yourself, and run a separate ballot line for each category. Add a panel of three or five judges, at least two of whom manage nobody in the room.

faqs.question: How should judges break a tie in a costume contest?
faqs.answer: Count the top marks first: the most +2 scores on an evaluation ballot, or the most first places on a ranked one. If the entries are still level, let the two entrants share the award.

faqs.question: What prizes work for a Halloween costume contest on a small budget?
faqs.answer: At no cost, make the winner's photo the team channel banner for a week. Under about $5 (EST, October 2026), spray-paint a plastic skull gold as a trophy; give things rather than cash.

faqs.question: Should young children be ranked in a costume contest?
faqs.answer: Not under about 8. Give every child a named ribbon, such as Kindest Monster or The Bookworm Ribbon, so the award describes the costume instead of ranking the child.

faqs.question: What costume contest categories should I avoid?
faqs.answer: Avoid anything that ranks bodies, such as Sexiest or Best Body, and anything about weight, height or skin. Skip Worst Costume too, and keep gore out of office and school contests.

faqs.question: Can SubhSandesh run a costume contest or a voting page?
faqs.answer: No. Each SubhSandesh Halloween page is made for one recipient and has no voting feature. It works as a thank-you to the organiser or a winner after the contest, not as the contest itself.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Costume Contest Categories: 36 Award Names by Setting

The best Halloween costume contest categories match the room: five to eight awards for an office, a named ribbon for every young child at school, and a no-costume "best effort" prize everywhere. Announce them early but expect late decisions. At Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival SubhSandesh has measured (n = 89 pages), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the day itself.

Judge for the screen as well as the room, because 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone and most contest photos will be seen small. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. Below: 36 original award names in five settings, three ballots, a judging panel plan, prizes by budget and four inclusion rules.

## What is a costume contest category?

A costume contest category is a named award with one judging question, such as "which costume tells the best story in 20 seconds?". Each category gets its own ballot line, so one popular guest cannot sweep every prize.

The trade runs it this way too. When the Halloween & Costume Association launched its first Spooky Awards, [Toy Book reported on 2 May 2024](https://toybook.com/hca-spooky-awards-2024-news/) that costume entries were split into six subcategories, including Child, Licensed and Scary/Horror. A panel of industry judges scored them on five criteria: Innovation, Marketability, Trendsetting Potential, Appeal and Usefulness.

## 36 Halloween costume contest categories and award names, by setting

Every name below is ours. Each setting lists awards, judges, ballot and award count.

### 1. Office: 8 award names

- **The Out-of-Office Award:** a costume that still works at a desk all afternoon.
- **Reply-All Horror:** the scariest costume, judged on craft, never gore.
- **The Quarterly Pun Report:** the best wordplay.
- **Department Possession Prize:** three or more colleagues dressed as one idea.
- **The Stationery Cupboard Cup:** a costume made only from office supplies.
- **The Commute Survivor:** a costume that made it in by train or bus intact.
- **The Inside Joke Award:** a costume the whole floor gets without context.
- **Best Effort Badge:** one accessory counts; no outfit change needed.

**Judges and ballot:** three judges from outside the biggest team, plus an approval ballot. **Awards:** five to eight, so no department wins most.

### 2. School and classroom: 7 award names

- **The Bookworm Ribbon:** the best character from a book.
- **Brightest Idea:** the most original idea a child chose alone.
- **Science Fair Fright:** something real, such as a planet, volcano or jellyfish.
- **Kindest Monster:** the friendliest scary costume.
- **The Story Spinner:** the best 20-second story, told by the child.
- **The Teamwork Trophy:** a class, sibling or friendship set.
- **Staff Room Special:** the best teacher costume, voted by pupils.

**Judges and ballot:** staff from another class. **Awards:** under 8, every child gets one of these names, so the ribbon describes rather than ranks.

### 3. Family party: 7 award names

- **The Three Generations Award:** a costume linking grandparent, parent and child.
- **Pet Parade Prize:** a pet costume the animal tolerates calmly.
- **The Kitchen Cupboard Cup:** a costume made from household items.
- **Tiny Terror:** given to every guest under 5.
- **The Accidental Match:** two guests who dressed alike without planning.
- **The Hand-Me-Down Hero:** a costume reworked from an older sibling's.
- **The Family Legend:** the costume with the best family story behind it.

**Judges and ballot:** the two oldest guests, plus a ranked top-three ballot. **Awards:** four to seven.

### 4. Bar or adult party: 7 award names

- **The Deep Cut:** the most obscure reference someone still recognised.
- **The Plot Twist:** a costume with a reveal, such as a cape that turns.
- **Lights-Down Award:** the best costume that glows in a dim room.
- **Bartender's Pick:** chosen by staff, who know nobody's friends.
- **The Dance Floor Licence:** a costume you can still dance and sit in.
- **The Crossover Episode:** two guests from different stories posing as a pair.
- **The Thrift Wizard:** a costume with a total spend under $20 (EST).

**Judges and ballot:** staff plus one guest drawn at random, plus an approval ballot. **Awards:** three to five, with an entry number on every costume.

### 5. Virtual contest: 7 award names

- **The Frame Filler:** the costume that uses the webcam frame best.
- **Background Bonus:** costume and virtual background working together.
- **The Mute Button Mime:** a costume explained without speaking.
- **Pet Cameo Prize:** the best animal guest appearance.
- **The Torch Trick:** the best lighting from a desk lamp or phone torch.
- **Time Zone Hero:** a costume worn at an awkward local hour.
- **The Buffering Award:** the best glitch-themed costume.

**Judges and ballot:** an evaluation ballot in a shared form, scored from screenshots. **Awards:** four to seven.

## How to vote: approval, evaluation or ranked ballots

The ballot can change the winner. In a field trial during the 2002 French presidential election, [Laslier and Van der Straeten (Experimental Economics, 2008)](https://hal.science/hal-00363212v1) found approval voting easily understood and well accepted, and it changed the overall ranking of candidates compared with the official single-choice vote.

A 2007 follow-up by [Baujard and Igersheim (2011)](https://shs.hal.science/halshs-00564256v1) also tested an evaluation ballot, where each candidate gets +2, +1 or 0. Participants said they wanted more expression and transparency than a single vote allowed. Both are election studies, read from their abstracts, but a costume vote is a small election.

Match the ballot to crowd size and format. Three work well:

- **Approval ballot:** tick every entry number you like; suits rooms of 20 or more.
- **Evaluation ballot (+2, +1, 0):** mark every entry; suits panels and virtual forms.
- **Ranked top three (3, 2 and 1 points):** suits a family party with under 15 entries.

Voters write entry numbers, not names, and never their own. Break a tie on the count of top marks (+2s or first places); if still level, the two share the award.

## Judging panels: why three neutral judges beat one boss

One judge who knows the entrants is a bias with a clipboard. [Myers and colleagues (Journal of Sports Science and Medicine, 2006)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3863918) studied 70 bouts at the 2003 IFMA MuayThai World Championships, each scored by five to nine judges, and found judges favoured their own country's fighters by about 1.09 points per bout.

With many neutral judges on each bout, the bias rarely changed a result. Office friendships are a small version of national loyalty, so build the panel the same way:

- three or five judges, never an even number;
- at least two who manage nobody in the room;
- a judge sits out any category their own team enters;
- with three judges, the middle score counts.

## Contest formats compared by setting

The five settings side by side. Prize budgets are our US-dollar estimates, October 2026.

| Setting | Award names | Ballot | Judges | Prize per award (EST) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Office | 8 | Approval | 3 neutral | $0–20 |
| School (under 8) | 7, one per child | None; every child named | Staff from another class | $0–3 |
| Family party | 7 | Ranked top three | 2 oldest guests | $0–10 |
| Bar or adult party | 7 | Approval, entry numbers | Staff plus 1 random guest | $10–50 |
| Virtual | 7 | Evaluation (+2, +1, 0) | 3, from screenshots | $0–15, posted |

The bigger and less familiar the crowd, the more the ballot matters. Small family rooms can rely on a ranked card.

## Prize ideas by budget (EST, October 2026)

Give things, not cash. Figures are typical US retail estimates for October 2026, not quotes.

- **$0:** the winner's photo as the team channel banner for a week, or a "costume consultant" title for next year.
- **Under $5:** a plastic skull spray-painted gold as a trophy, or glow sticks for school winners.
- **$5–20:** a framed print of the winning photo, or a book matching the costume's character.
- **$20–50:** a team lunch for a group category, or a kit for next year (wig, face paint, mask).

Virtual winners need postage on top, about $5–10 per US parcel (EST). Send prizes within a week, while the screenshots are still circulating.

## Inclusion: 4 rules every category list needs

Categories decide who feels welcome before anyone votes. Four rules cover most of it:

- **Keep a no-costume category.** The Best Effort Badge lets someone join with one accessory, so people who skip Halloween for faith or personal reasons still belong.
- **Do not rank children under 8.** Every child gets a named ribbon instead.
- **Judge costumes, never bodies.** Drop "Sexiest", "Best Body", anything about weight, height or skin, and "Worst Costume".
- **Keep scary opt-in.** Reply-All Horror judges craft; gore stays out of office and school contests.

## Thanking one winner: where SubhSandesh fits

SubhSandesh does not run contests, count votes or print ribbons. Each Halloween page is written for exactly one recipient, which makes it a thank-you tool: the organiser who printed every ballot, or the colleague who took the Best Effort Badge.

The [interactive Halloween card with photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes, holds up to six photos and ends with a 1080×1920 Boo License. For more, the [premium Halloween page with a voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and a reply box.

Either can be password-protected, as 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators do before sharing. For a thank-you with no Halloween theme, [browse every SubhSandesh template](https://subhsandesh.in/templates); the pages are English only, a poor fit for a winner who reads another language.

## When a costume contest is the wrong call

Skip it when fewer than a third of the group plans to dress up, because the same three people will collect every prize. A team mid-redundancy, or a school where many families avoid Halloween, is better served by a costume-optional party without awards.

For an office, hold it on Friday 30 October 2026 or Friday 29 October 2027, inside working hours. After hours, it can feel like unpaid overtime.

## Sources

- Toy Book, "Trick or Trophy: Halloween & Costume Association Hosts First Spooky Awards", 2 May 2024.
- Laslier and Van der Straeten, "A live experiment on approval voting", Experimental Economics, 2008 (abstract read).
- Baujard and Igersheim, "A Framed-field experiment on Approval voting and Evaluation voting", 2011 (abstract read).
- Myers, Balmer, Nevill and Al-Nakeeb, "Evidence of nationalistic bias in muaythai", Journal of Sports Science and Medicine, 2006 (abstract read).
- SubhSandesh platform data, measured 9 and 24 September 2026.

structuralLimitations: SERP is mostly hijacked-subdomain spam (6 of 9 results); only cheddarup (snippet), ualberta (404) and toybook were real pages, so the Phase 1 table rests on snippets for two of three.

Overlap with b6 halloween-costume-party-ideas: that post already recommends an approval ballot, one parade, a 10-point score and the Antipov 2017 order-effects paper. Both voting papers study national elections, not party contests; the post says so in the body.
Toy Book ranks #6 for the keyword (not top 5); it is a trade-news report of the HCA announcement, not a competitor. HCA's own page was not fetched (search budget).
Prices are labelled US retail estimates (EST, October 2026), not quotes.
